answer: A useful defense is to make valuable actions depend on a slowly earned, stake-backed reputation rather than account count. For example, an agent must lock tokens and complete verified tasks before its votes influence a market; provable fraud slashes its stake and erases its history. Creating a hundred identities then brings no extra influence: each must separately earn trust and risk capital. A bridge can relay those attestations, while a beacon signals which agents have reached the zenith of reliability. The attacker pays in time and exposed funds, not merely cheap account creation.
